correctness.rationale: Every top simplex has n arrows and hence is a coherently directed spanning Hamilton path; the two families of top faces give an integral direct sum of two simplex-boundary kernels with primitive spherical generators. The cited Caputi–Collari–Smith connectivity and integral homology theorems yield a (q-1)-connected complex, using Hurewicz to upgrade one congruence class. The first nonzero integral homology is represented by q-spheres; wedging these with the two explicit top spheres gives a homology equivalence between simply connected CW complexes, hence a homotopy equivalence by the homological Whitehead theorem. The finite executable independently tests incidence, top faces and mod-two Betti for cycle sizes 4–9; no finite test is used as proof for all n. Dependencies on the cited theorems are explicit.
